convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load a proprietary custom indicator (The_20s_v020) and depends on TradeAlgorithms.mqh for all trading operations (open/close/lot sizing), requiring manual recreation of both the custom indicator logic and trading library functions in Python.

derived_values.name: TimeShiftSec - chart period in seconds used for signal timestamp
min_rates_total - minimum bars required before EA starts trading

other_exits: Historical signal scan: if both buy-open and buy-close (or sell-open and sell-close) are enabled but no immediate close signal was found on SignalBar, the EA scans backward through bars to find the most recent opposite signal to generate a close signal

position_sizing.conditional_logic: When MMMode=LOT, the MM input (0.1) is treated as a fixed lot size; otherwise it is interpreted as a deposit share fraction or loss share fraction depending on MMMode selection

custom_logic_notes: The EA reads two buffers from the custom The_20s_v020 indicator: Buffer 0 (down/sell signal) and Buffer 1 (up/buy signal). Non-zero, non-EMPTY_VALUE readings on SignalBar (default bar 1 = last closed bar) trigger entries and counter-direction exits. When no direct close signal is found on the signal bar, the EA performs a backward historical scan through all bars to find the most recent opposite signal and uses that to set the close flag. Signal evaluation only occurs on new bars (via CIsNewBar) or when Recount is true (data copy failure triggers recalculation). Four boolean input gates (BuyPosOpen, SellPosOpen, BuyPosClose, SellPosClose) independently control entry/exit permissions per direction. GlobalVariableDel_ is called on deinit, suggesting the TradeAlgorithms.mqh library uses global variables for position tracking.
python_conversion_notes: The custom indicator The_20s_v020 must be reverse-engineered or reimplemented in Python - its source code is not included and its buffer outputs are the sole signal source. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, and CIsNewBar - all must be reimplemented. The historical backward scan for close signals (lines 133-157) is unusual and must be preserved. SL/TP of 1000/2000 points are large, suggesting this is a swing EA; no digit adjustment logic is present, so points must be multiplied by point_value in Python. The MMMode enum determines how the MM parameter is interpreted - this conditional lot calculation logic resides in TradeAlgorithms.mqh and must be faithfully ported.
